uttara.64.5: ‘O brave one, keep the army that is well-formed, in such good cheer that its constituents are happy and satisfied, and not arrogant, with your good words. (4-5)
uttara.64.6: ‘There (at the encounter) neither wealth nor spouse, nor even relatives are at your side, as the servants when kept happy. (6)
uttara.64.7: ‘Thus, having dispatched the mighty army full of happy men, you alone, with bow in your hand, can go to the forest of Madhu. (7)
uttara.64.8: ‘You should go in a manner in which the son of Madhu, Lavaṇa does not know that you are going to him for an encounter. (8)
uttara.64.9: ‘O bull among men, there is indeed no other way in which Lavaṇa would die, whosoever goes to attack him, is killed by Lavaṇa, indeed. (9)
uttara.64.10: ‘Thus when summer is passed, and the rainy season comes, you should kill Lavaṇa. O graceful one, that is the time of death for this wicked one. (10)
uttara.64.11: ‘Your warriors may proceed with the great Ṛṣis at their head, so that by the end of the summer season, they may cross the Gaṅgā, the daughter of Jāhnu. (11)
uttara.64.12: ‘Then having stationed your army at the banks there, O one of speedy steps, you go ahead carefully alone with the bow.’ (12)
uttara.64.13: Thus being spoken to by Śrī Rāma, Śatrughna, having gathered together the brave chiefs of the army spoke thus to them: (13)
uttara.64.14: ‘These are the decided places where you can dwell, according to your liking; wherever you are stay amicably.’ (14)
uttara.64.15: Thus ordering them and despatching the mighty army, he made obeisance to Kausalyā, Sumitrā and Kaikeyī. (15)
uttara.64.17: Paying salutation to Śrī Rāma with his head and going round Him, and falling at the feet of Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, and the chief priest Vasiṣṭha, Śatrughna of pious mind, the torturer of the foes, the mighty one going round Śrī Rāma again, departed. (16-17)
uttara.64.18: Sending ahead the army then, full of elephants and horses, he himself lived there with Śrī Rāma for a month and then he too started. (18)
uttara.65.1: Despatching the entire army, residing for a month only in Ayodhyā on his way, Śatrughna alone proceeded in haste. (1)
uttara.65.2: After spending two nights on the way, Śatrughna, descendant of the Raghus, reached the holy hermitage of Vālmīki, the best of the places to dwell. (2)
uttara.65.3: Śatrughna after saluting him with folded hands spoke these words to Vālmīki, the best among the ascetics: (3)
uttara.65.4: ‘Sir, I desire to stay here; I have come for a mighty purpose. I shall go tomorrow morning to the west, the quarter of Varuṇa.’ (4)
uttara.65.5: Having heard those words of Śatrughna, the best among the ascetics, Vālmīki, said cheerfully to him (Śatrughna), the noble one: “Welcome to thee, O famous one. (5)
uttara.65.6: “O gracious one, this hermitage is indeed your own, the family of the descendants of Raghu. Accept without hesitation the Pādya (ablutions of the foot), Arghya and the seat offered by me.” (6)
uttara.65.7: Accepting then the homage and the fruits and the roots, the scion of Kakutstha, took the food and was fully satisfied. (7)
uttara.65.8: Having taken the fruits and the roots, he (Śatrughna) said to that great Ṛṣi: ‘To whom belong all these accoutrements of sacrifice that are seen on the eastern side, close to the hermitage’ (8)
uttara.65.9: Hearing these words of Śatrughna, Vālmīki spoke out: “O Śatrughna! listen as to whom this place of sacrifice belonged formerly. (9)
uttara.65.10: “Among your ancestors there was Saudāsa, and of that king, was a son named Vīrasaha, who was very brave and extremely pious. (10)
uttara.65.11: “Although young, yet valiant Saudāsa went out for hunting in forest and saw two Rākṣasas roaming about. (11)
uttara.65.12: “Those two Rākṣasas assuming the dreadful shape of the lion and devouring many thousands of animals, yet they were still unsatiated. (12)
uttara.65.13: “Seeing those two Rākṣasas and the forest devoid of animals, he, Saudāsa, was enraged and killed one of them with a mighty shaft. (13)
uttara.65.14: “Having killed one of the Rākṣasas the bull among men, Saudāsa, without worry and anger looked at the slain Rākṣasa. (14)
uttara.65.16: “Having seen the dead Rākṣasa, his comrade was greatly pained and said to Saudāsa: ‘As you have killed that Rākṣasa, a friend of mine, who was not at all guilty, so O sinful one, I shall take my revenge on you.” (15-16)
uttara.65.17: Having said so, that Rākṣasa disappeared. After the lapse of some time, Mitrasaha (Vīrasaha) became the king of Ayodhyā. (17)
uttara.65.18: The king also performed the great sacrifice, the Aśvamedha (horse-sacrifice) near the hermitage and Vasiṣṭha also participated in that sacrifice. (18)
uttara.65.19: The great sacrifice lasted for many years and was comparable with the sacrifice of the gods being performed with great pomp. (19)
uttara.65.20: Now at the end of this sacrifice, the Rākṣasa in the form of Vasiṣṭha remembering the former enmity spoke to the king. (20)
uttara.65.21: ‘At the conclusion of the last part of the sacrifice, give me immediately my food consisting of flesh, and do not ponder over this.’ (21)
uttara.65.22: Hearing those words, spoken by Rākṣasa in the form of Brāhmaṇa Vasiṣṭha, the king spoke to the expert cooks: (22)
uttara.65.23: ‘Prepare soon such food possessed of flesh, fatty and worthy of offering, so that our preceptor, Vasiṣṭha, is satisfied.’ (23)
uttara.65.24: The chief of the cooks was perturbed in mind at the orders of the king; then that Rākṣasa soon took the form of the cook. (24)
uttara.65.25: He brought human flesh to the king and said: “This tasteful food, possessed of flesh, has been brought by me.’ (25)
uttara.65.26: That best among men (Vīrasaha) together with his wife Madayantī offered this food possessed of flesh brought by the Rākṣasa to Vasiṣṭha. (26)
uttara.65.28: Knowing human flesh to have been brought as food, the Brāhmaṇa (Vasiṣṭha) possessed of great anger ventured to speak thus: ‘O king as you desire to give such food to me, so no doubt this shall be your food’. (27-28)
uttara.65.29: Then Saudāsa enraged by this, took up a hand-full of water and was on the point of cursing Vasiṣṭha; his wife, however, checked him. (29)
uttara.65.30: ‘As the holy Ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha is our venerable preceptor and a chief priest comparable to the gods, O king! so you cannot curse him in return.’ (30)
uttara.65.31: Then the pious Saudāsa employed the water held in his hand, which was infused with anger and his spiritual power and sprinkled his feet with it. (31)
uttara.65.33: By it (this sprinkling) the feet of the king became variegated in colour, and thence the king by name Saudāsa, became famous as Kalmāṣapāda (with feet of dark-variegated colour), and was so known. That King with his wife falling at the feet of Vasiṣṭha again and again repeated to Vasiṣṭha what was uttered by the Rākṣasa, in the form of a Brāhmaṇa. (32-33)
uttara.65.34: After having heard what the King said and knowing the food being contaminated by the Rākṣasa, Vasiṣṭḥa again spoke to Saudāsa, the bull among men: (34)
uttara.65.35: ‘These words that have been uttered by me in anger, cannot be rendered ineffective, I will, however, grant you a boon. (35)
uttara.65.36: The curse will come to an end after twelve years and by my grace, you will not remember the past.” (36)
uttara.65.37: Thus that King, the extirpator of enemies, having borne that curse, regained his kingdom and protected his subjects. (37)
uttara.65.38: ‘Of that Kalmāṣapāda is this holy place of sacrifice, near the hermitage about which you asked me’. (38)
uttara.65.39: Having heard this dreadful story of that king Kalmāṣapāda, Śatrughna saluted the great Ṛṣi and entered the hutment. (39)
uttara.66.1: During that night Śatrughna entered the arbour. The same very night Sītā gave birth to two sons. (1)
uttara.66.2: At midnight, the young ascetics spoke to sage Vālmīki about the auspicious motherhood of Sītā, which news very much pleased him: (2)
uttara.66.3: ‘Sir, the wife of Rāma has given birth to two sons. So, O powerful one, make the protecting rites that destroy the ill spirits of the nether world.’ (3)
uttara.66.4: Hearing these words from them, the great sage went there and saw the two sons, who were like sons of the gods and were as effulgent as the moon. (4)
uttara.66.5: The sage went there joyfully and looked at the two sons and made the sacrament for both of them that kills the inauspicous Bhūtas and destroys the Rākṣasa. (5)
uttara.66.6: That Brāhmaṇa Vālmīki took the handful of Kuśa and Lava (the lower portion of the Kuśa grass) and preparing the totemic device, handed it over to them, the protective symbol that kills the Bhūtas. (6)
uttara.66.7: ‘He who of the two was born first should be cleansed with the Kuśas purified by chants and then his name will be ‘Kuśa.’ (7)
uttara.66.8: ‘Who happens to be born later, should be cleansed carefully with Lava by the old women and will be known by the name of Lava. (8)
uttara.66.9: ‘Thus these twins named Kuśa and Lava will become famous bearing the names given by me.’ (9)
uttara.66.10: Then the old women of Āśrama pure in mind took with care the totemic device from the hands of the sage and performed the protective rites of the twins. (10)
uttara.66.12: While in this manner (the symbolic protection) was being performed by the old women, Śatrughna at midnight heard the joyful Gotra and name of Śrī Rāma and also the news of delivery of the two sons by Sītā and then having entered the arbour of Sītā said, ‘O mother, by the grace of God two sons are born to you.’ (11-12)
uttara.66.13: Then the night of the rainy season of the month of Śrāvaṇa (full moon) passed swiftly with noble Śatrughna enjoying himself. (13)
uttara.66.14: At break of dawn, having performed the morning ablutions, he (Śatrughna) taking leave of the sage with folded hands, started forth to the western direction. (14)
uttara.66.15: Reaching the banks of the Yamunā, and having spent seven nights on the way he (Śatrughna) made for his stay in the hermitages of the sages of holy fame. (15)
uttara.66.16: He, the famous one, dwelt there with the sages among whom Bhārgava was the foremost, taking part in talks proper to the occasion. (16)
uttara.66.17: This way the mightiest among Raghus and great souled Śatrughna in the company of sages like Cyavana passed that night through hearing various religious tales. (17)
uttara.67.2: Then as the night appeared, Śatrughna asked the Brāhmaṇa, Cyavana, son of Bhṛgu the exact might of Lavaṇa, and the power of the trident also. He enquired, ‘O Brāhmaṇa, who were killed by this special trident having entered into a duel with Lavaṇa.’ (1-2)
uttara.67.3: Hearing these words of the noble Śatrughna, the mighty Cyavana said in reply to the scion of the Raghus: (3)
uttara.67.4: ‘Among the innumerable doings of this Lavaṇa listen to me that which took place in the context of the originator of the family of Ikṣvāku (Māndhātā). (4)
uttara.67.5: ‘In the old days, there was a powerful king, the son of Yuvanāśva, known as Māndhātā, noted for his might in the three worlds. (5)
uttara.67.6: ‘Having ruled over the entire earth, that king, lord of the earth, embarked on a conquest of the world of the gods from here, the earth. (6)
uttara.67.7: ‘Great fear overcame Indra and other mighty gods, when Māndhātā prepared to fight with a desire to conquer the world of gods. (7)
uttara.67.8: Propitiated by the host of gods, Māndhātā, the king, having vowed to take one half of Indra’s kingdom and the other half of earthly sovereignty, went up to raid heaven. (8)
uttara.67.9: ‘Indra, the conqueror of Pāka Daitya, having known his evil intentions, uttered these conciliatory words to the progeny of Yuvanāśva. (9)
uttara.67.10: ‘O bull among men, Māndhātā, you are still not established as a king in the mortal worlds, and you desire the kingdom of the gods here without subjugating the earth. (10)
uttara.67.11: ‘O brave one, if the entire earth is indeed under your sway then you may rule over the kingdom of the gods together with your attendants, army and carriers. (11)
uttara.67.12: Māndhātā said to Indra: ‘O Indra, where does my rule over the earth is obstructed’? (12)
uttara.67.13: The thousand-eyed Indra told him, ‘O sinless one, the son of Madhu, the Rākṣasa Lavaṇa by name, does not obey your orders.’ (13)
uttara.67.14: Having heard the dreadful unpleasant words, conveyed by Indra, the King put to shame with face downcast, could not speak. (14)
uttara.67.15: Taking leave of the thousand-eyed god, with his face turned somewhat downwards, the lord of the mortals proceeded and came back again to this world. (15)
uttara.67.16: That king, the destroyer of foes, with anger in his heart and together with his attendants and carriers came to bring the son of Madhu, Lavaṇa, under his sway. (16)
uttara.67.17: Desirous to fight with Lavaṇa, the bull among men, Māndhātā, sent a messenger to Lavaṇa. (17)
uttara.67.18: He, the messenger, having approached the son of Madhu, said many unpleasant words; the Rākṣasa devoured that messenger while he was speaking thus. (18)
uttara.67.19: The messenger, on being late in returning, the King possessed of anger, inflicted injury on the Rākṣasa by shower of arrows on all sides. (19)
uttara.67.20: Then that Rākṣasa laughed and took the trident in his hand and released the best among weapons, the trident, for the purpose of slaying Māndhātā with all his followers. (20)
uttara.67.21: That enflamed trident on its part, having rendered to ashes the king together with his attendant, army and carriers—came back to the hand of Lavaṇa. (21)
uttara.67.22: Thus that great King was killed together with his army and carriers, O gracious one, the power of the trident is impossible to fathom. (22)
uttara.67.23: Tomorrow morning, you shall soon kill Lavaṇa while he is without the weapon, there is no doubt that your victory is certain. (23)
uttara.67.25: By you performing this deed the welfare of the worlds will be achieved. Thus all has been narrated to you, O bull among men, about the might of the wicked Lavaṇa and the unfathomable dreadful power of the trident, O king Māndhātā; Lavaṇa perished due to his own misdeeds. (24-25)
uttara.67.26: Tomorrow morning you will slay Lavaṇa I have no doubt, O noble one, when he will proceed for flesh, having not the trident with him, victory shall be yours, O king of men. (26)
uttara.68.1: The night passed away quickly while staying at the hermitage of Cyavana, the noble Śatrughna conversing with Cyavana and other sages, who wished for his holy victory (against Lavaṇa). (1)
uttara.68.2: Then in the morning when it was dawn, that Rākṣasa, Lavaṇa, the heroic one, went out of his city impelled by the desire to bring his food. (2)
uttara.68.3: In the meantime, Śatrughna, the brave one, having crossed the Yamunā, stood at the gates of the city of Madhu, with bow in his hand. (3)
uttara.68.4: Then at midday that Rākṣasa, Lavaṇa, the evil-doer returned bearing the load of many thousand creatures. (4)
uttara.68.5: Then the Rākṣasa saw Śatrughna armed with the bow, standing at the gate and said to him: ‘What will you do with this weapon? (5)
uttara.68.6: ‘Many thousands of men like you accompanied with weapons, O wretched one, have been devoured by me in anger. Death seems to have come nearer to you. (6)
uttara.68.7: ‘O vile one, my food is yet incomplete, having come, you enter my mouth of your own accord?’ (7)
uttara.68.8: While the Rākṣasa spoke thus and laughing, the heroic Śatrughna broke in tears with anger. (8)
uttara.68.9: Fiery rays issued forth from all the limbs of the noble and angry Śatrughna. (9)
uttara.68.10: Highly enraged, Śatrughna then addressed the demon, who roamed about thus at right, ‘O evil one, I wish to have a duel with you. (10)
uttara.68.11: ‘I am the son of (King) Daśaratha, and the brother of the wise Śrī Rāma, the extirpator of foes, Śatrughna by name. I have come with a desire to kill you. (11)
uttara.68.12: ‘So give the duel to me, who desires to fight with you! You are the enemy of all beings; with me alive here you shall not escape.’ (12)
uttara.68.13: When Śatrughna had spoken thus, that Rākṣasa, Lavaṇa, replied to the best among men, as if laughing: ‘O wicked one, it is my good luck that you have come within my reach. (13)
uttara.68.14: ‘O insensate one, the Rākṣasa Rāvaṇa the brother of my maternal aunt, was killed by Rāma for the sake of a woman. (14)
uttara.68.15: All I had forgiven, the destruction of the family of Rāvaṇa, and ignoring specially you. (15)
uttara.68.16: ‘But now all of you, that have been born or will be born and even you vile ones, will be swept away by me like straws. (16)
uttara.68.17: ‘I shall indeed give you a fight, who wish it, O fool of vicious intellect. Just wait for a moment, while I bring my weapon (trident). (17)
uttara.68.18: ‘I am going to be equipped with the weapon with which I desire to kill you.’ At this Śatrughna at once spoke out: ‘Where will you go as long as I am alive? (18)
uttara.68.19: ‘The enemy that has come of his own accord does not deserve to be set free by one disciplined in mind. Whoever with unsettled mind gives freedom to a foe to disappear, that weak-minded one indeed would be killed as a coward. (19)
uttara.68.20: ‘You, therefore, have a good look at this world of mortals, O wicked one! I shall carry you to Yama’s abode with many sharp arrows, O foe of the three worlds and also of Raghu’s family.’ (20)
uttara.69.1: Hearing these words of the noble Śatrughna, Lavaṇa became extremely angry and said: ‘Wait for a moment’. (1)
uttara.69.2: Rubbing his one hand with the other, and making a rattling sound with his teeth, Lavaṇa challenged the lion among Raghus many times. (2)
uttara.69.3: To that Lavaṇa of fearful appearance, speaking thus, Śatrughna, the killer of the enemies of the gods, said these words: (3)
uttara.69.4: ‘Śatrughna was not born, when others were conquered by you in battle, so go to the abode of Yama today, killed by my arrow. (4)
uttara.69.5: ‘O sinful one, may the sages too see you killed in encounter today, also the learned Brāhmaṇas, as the gods saw Rāvaṇa killed. (5)
uttara.69.6: ‘Today there will be peace indeed in the city and province, as you, the demon roaming about at night are slain by my arrow and lie prostrate on the ground and burnt. (6)
uttara.69.7: ‘Today, the arrow, whose fore-point resembles the thunderbolt, released by my hand, shall enter your heart as the ray of the sun enters in the lotus.’ (7)
uttara.69.8: Being thus spoken, Lavaṇa enraged with anger threw a mightly tree on the breast of Śatrughna; but Śatrughna cut it thousandfold with arrows. (8)
uttara.69.9: Thus seeing his action fruitless, the powerful Rākṣasa again taking hold of many trees hurled them at Śatrughna. (9)
uttara.69.10: The brave Śatrughna too, tore asunder each one coming upon him, by three or four arrows of flatterend ends. (10)
uttara.69.11: Thus, Śatrughna then possessed of great might, let loose a shower of arrows on the Rākṣasa; however, the Rākṣasa was not troubled. (11)
uttara.69.12: Then the powerful Lavaṇa laughed, and lifting a tree attacked the brave one, Śatrughna, on the head; Śatrughna went into a swoon with the bodily joints loosened. (12)
uttara.69.13: So, as the brave Śatrughna fell, long cries of ‘Hā’ emanated from the sages, the host of the gods, the Gandharvas and Apsarās (the celestial beings). (13)
uttara.69.14: Ignoring Śatrughna, fallen on the ground whom he took killed, the Rākṣasa did not enter his residence, although given time to do so. (14)
uttara.69.15: Nor even did he, Lavaṇa, take up the trident seeing him (Śatrughna) lying on the ground, and then considering him, Śatrughna, dead, carried again his provisions. (15)
uttara.69.16: Gaining consciousness in a moment, Śatrughna, adored by the sages, stood up and waited at the door of the city of Madhu, weapon in his hand. (16)
uttara.69.20: Then Śatrughna took hold of the arrow: the divine and excelling others, flaming with brilliance and filling the ten quarters with its brilliance, shaped like the thunderbolt in front, resembling the thunderbolt in speed, equalling Meru and Mandara mountains, flat shaped, invincible in all encounters, smeared with red sandal-like blood, beautiful as the winged bird, dreadful for the lord of the Dānavas and also the mountains, resembling as if the fire of destruction kindled at the time of final dissolution. Seeing it, all beings were very much frightened. (17—20)
uttara.69.21: The whole world, together with the Devas, Asuras and Gandharvas and the sages, was in discomfort and all approached Pitāmaha (Brahmā). (21)
uttara.69.22: They narrated to the god of the gods, Prapitāmaha Brahmā, the bewilderment of the gods with fear regarding the security of the worlds. (22)
uttara.69.23: ‘O lord ! is the destruction of the world at hand or has the end of the universe approached? O grand sire, never before has such a condition of the world been seen or heard.’ (23)
uttara.69.24: Hearing their words, Brahmā the grandfather of the worlds, protector of the gods, revealed the cause of the fear of the gods. (24)
uttara.69.25: He said in a sweet voice: ‘All the gods listen to me; the arrow has been held by Śatrughna for the slaying of Lavaṇa in encounter. (25)
uttara.69.28: ‘All the great gods are bewildered at the power of that arrow ! O my children, this is the eternal powerful arrow of the former God, the creator of the world, Viṣṇu, due to which the gods are in fear; this mighty arrow was created for the destruction of those two sons of Diti, Madhu and Kaiṭabha; Viṣṇu alone knows well about this powerful arrow. (26—28)
uttara.69.33: ‘This arrow is the ancient form of the noble Viṣṇu; go from here, O my children, and witness Lavaṇa being killed by the noble and heroic Śatrughna, the younger brother of Śrī Rāma.’ The gods hearing the words of the God of gods, came to the place where both Śatrughna and Lavaṇa were engaged in fighting; all beings witnessed that divine arrow borne by Śatrughna in his hand, as if it was the fire that broke out at the time of universal destruction. Seeing the sky filled with the gods, Śatrughna, again having roared like a loin, looked at Lavaṇa; he (Lavaṇa) was again challenged by the noble Śatrughna. (29—33)
uttara.69.36: Lavaṇa filled with anger appeared to give him (Śatrughna) the fight. He, Śatrughna, the best among archers, then having stretched that bow up to his ear, shot the arrow at the mighty chest of Lavaṇa. That divine arrow descended to the nether-world breaking open Lavaṇa’s chest, and having gone there, being worshipped by the gods, came back quickly again to Śatrughna, the descendant of the family of Ikṣvāku. (34—36)
uttara.69.37: That demon Lavaṇa being struck by the arrow of Śatrughna, fell on the ground all at once like the mountain struck by the thunderbolt. (37)
uttara.69.38: On the Rākṣasa Lavaṇa being killed, that mighty divine arrow too, came back to the quiver of Rudra as all the gods looked on. (38)
uttara.69.40: Then the champion of Raghus, Śatrughna, felled with one arrow the terror of three worlds, shone forth as the sun dispelling the darkness. All gods, sages, serpents paid homage to him and Apsarās hailed the fearless victory of the son of Śrī Daśaratha, the serpent laid to rest. (39-40)
uttara.70.1: After Lavaṇa was killed, the gods, together with Indra and Agni as their head, spoke these sweet words to Śatrughna, the tormentor of the foes. (1)
uttara.70.2: ‘O lion among men, by good fortune, victory is yours and the Rākṣasa is dead, O! of a noble vow! ask us for a boon. (2)
uttara.70.3: ‘All desirous of your victory are intending to grant boon to you. We have come; our presence here will not be fruitless.’ (3)
uttara.70.4: Hearing the words of the gods, Śatrughna, the long-armed one, disciplined in mind, keeping his folded hands on his head replied thus : (4)
uttara.70.5: ‘This city of Madhu, Madhurā by name, built by the gods, may become the capital soon. This is the only boon that I desire: (5)
uttara.70.6: The gods said: ‘So be it’ O scion of the Raghus: This beautiful city will be Śūrasenā indeed, possessed of an army of brave men, there is no doubt about it.’ (6)
uttara.70.7: Thus saying the holy gods then ascended to heaven. Śatrughna too, the powerful one, brought back the army from the banks of the Gaṅgā. (7)
uttara.70.8: That army came soon, hearing the news of the death of Lavaṇa at the hands of Śatrughna and commenced the establishment of the capital in the month of Śrāvaṇa (roughly corresponding to July-August). (8)
uttara.70.9: That holy country was established as the territory of the Śūrasenas, in the course of twelve years, as there was no cause for fear. (9)
uttara.70.10: The fields were full with grains, Indra (the rain-god) brought forth rain in time, the warriors, protected by Śatrughna, were free of disease. (10)
uttara.70.11: That city, shaped like the half-moon, beautified by the banks of the Yamunā, was also embellished with special mansions and quadrangular market-place. It was inhabited by the four Varṇas (castes) and abounded in all forms of merchandise and trade. (11)
uttara.70.13: The white mansion that was formerly built by Lavaṇa, Śatrughna further beautified with pictures of various colours, looking beautiful on all sides with rest-houses and Vihāras, and that city was adorned with human and celestial embellishments. (12-13)
uttara.70.15: The prosperous Śatrughna, the younger brother of Bharata, having seen the city, divine in appearance, filled with all forms of merchandise and inhabited by traders coming from various countries, was much pleased. (14-15)
uttara.70.16: Then at the commencement of the twelfth year, having established the city Madhurā, he thought ‘I shall see the feet of Śrī Rāma.’ (16)
uttara.70.17: Then establishing that city, resembling a celestial one, Śatrughna filling it with men of various types, the enhancer of Raghu’s family, considered it appropriate to see Śrī Rāma’s feet. (17)
uttara.71.1: Then in the twelfth year Śatrughna, followed by a few attendants and the army, desired to proceed to Ayodhyā, ruled over by Śrī Rāma. (1)
uttara.71.2: Then making the army-chiefs and the councillors to retreat, he (Śatrughna) proceeded riding on a special horse, accompanied by a hundred chariots. (2)
uttara.71.3: Śatrughna, the descendant of the Raghus, possessed of fame, halting at seven to eight places on the way, reached the hermitage of Vālmīki and dwelt there. (3)
uttara.71.4: Having paid obeisance at the feet of sage Vālmīki, the famous Śatrughna accepted ablutions, offerings and hospitality from the sage. (4)
uttara.71.5: The sage, Vālmīki, narrated to the noble Śatrughna sweet tales of various themes. (5)
uttara.71.6: Referring to the killing of Lavaṇa, the sage said: ‘By killing Lavaṇa, a difficult task has been accomplished by you. (6)
uttara.71.7: ‘O gracious one, of long-arms, many powerful kings, together with their army and carriers had been killed by Lavaṇa, when they came in encounter with him. (7)
uttara.71.8: ‘O Bull among men, that evil one has been killed by you with ease, and by your prowess, the fright of worlds due to him has been dispelled. (8)
uttara.71.9: ‘The dreadful killing of Rāvaṇa by Śrī Rāma was achieved with great effort; this great task of killing Lavaṇa was performed by you without effort. (9)
uttara.71.10: ‘On Lavaṇa being killed, the gods are highly pleased. This admirable deed for all beings and the world has been performed by you. (10)
uttara.71.11: ‘That encounter with Lavaṇa was indeed seen by me, as it ensued, while I was sitting in the assembly of Vāsava (Indra), O bull among men. (11)
uttara.71.12: ‘My heart too, O Śatrughna, is filled with joy; I shall smell the crown of your head as this is the highest course of affection.’ (12)
uttara.71.13: Thus saying and smelling the crown of the head of Śatrughna, the wise one, Vālmīki, offered hospitality to him and all those who followed him. (13)
uttara.71.15: That jewel among men, Śatrughna, took the food offered by Vālmīki; then heard the deeds of Śrī Rāma, as they were performed by Him at that time melodiously, accompanied with the sound of the lute with proper beats and the three musical tunes manifested at proper beats, and at proper places, in Sanskrit, and according to the rules of music and also with the beat of drums at proper intervals. (14-15)
uttara.71.16: Śatrughna heard the deeds of Śrī Rāma as they were performed formerly, those words (comprising the song) were true and narrated as per the deeds performed in sequence. (16)
uttara.71.17: Having heard the story duly sung, the lion among men, Śatrughna, with tears in his eyes, was rendered unconscious, and fell into a swoon immediately taking deep sighs repeatedly. (17)
uttara.71.19: Śatrughna heard the deeds sung as if they were performed in the present. The warriors, who followed him, on hearing the rich song, were overwhelmed and speechless, indeed, and exclaimed to each other—‘How wonderful it is’. (18-19)
uttara.71.20: ‘What is this, where are we, have we been in a dream, that thing, which we had seen formerly, we see again in the hermitage. (20)
uttara.71.21: ‘Do we hear in dream this beautifully composed song’ filled with great surprise, they said to Śatrughna: (21)
uttara.71.24: ‘Please ask Vālmīki, O best among men, who composed this song? Śatrughna on his part, told all the warriors filled with surprise: ‘Here I am not able to ask Vālmīki in this manner, many wonders exist here in this hermitage of the sage, it is not proper to go and question the great sage out of curiosity.’ Thus having spoken to the warriors, the scion of the Raghus then having saluted the great sage, started for his apartment. (22—24)
uttara.72.1: Śatrughna, a tiger among men, could not sleep in the night ruminating over the song of Rāma’s deeds, full of meaning. (1)
uttara.72.2: Night passed away for the noble Śatrughna quickly, hearing the melodious sound of the song accompanied with that of the Vīṇā (lute) with proper beats. (2)
uttara.72.3: After the night had ended, Śatrughna with folded hands said to Vālmīki, the best among sages, having performed the morning duties: (3)
uttara.72.4: ‘Sir, I wish to see Śrī Rāma, the scion of the Raghus, with your permission and also that of these sages, firmly adhering to their vowes.’ (4)
uttara.72.5: Thus talking, Vālmīki embraced Śatrughna, the extirpator of foes, the scion of the Raghus, and let him go. (5)
uttara.72.6: Saluting Vālmīki, the best among sages, he, Śatrughna, ascending the shining chariot, went on speedily to Ayodhyā, eager to see the scion of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma. (6)
uttara.72.7: The descendant of Ikṣvāku, the prosperous one, Śatrughna, reached the city, Ayodhyā, and entered the king’s palace where Śrī Rāma, the illustrious one, was. (7)
uttara.72.9: Seeing Śrī Rāma with a face like full moon, seated among the councillors like Indra among the gods, and as if enflamed with vigour, Śatrughna with folded hands spoke to resplendant one after saluting Him: (8-9)
uttara.72.10: ‘All that you ordered me to do, I have done; the evil Lavaṇa has been killed and the city, Madhupurī, has been reinstituted. (10)
uttara.72.11: ‘These twelve years I have spent without you. O king, I cannot now live afar, separated from you. (11)
uttara.72.12: ‘O scion of the Kakutsthas, possessed of unmitigated power, give me thy favour, I cannot live without you for long, like a child separated from its mother.’ (12)
uttara.72.13: Then the scion of the Kakutsthas, Śrī Rāma, embraced him, Śatrughna, who spoke thus and said: ‘O brave one, do not lose heart, this does not become a Kṣatriya. (13)
uttara.72.14: ‘O descendant of Raghu, Śatrughna, the Kings staying away from their kingdom are not disheartened; the subjects are indeed to be protected as laid down among duties for the Kṣatriya. (14)
uttara.72.15: ‘O brave one, come from time to time again to Ayodhyā to see me. O best among men, you should go to your city, the city of Madhurā. (15)
uttara.72.16: ‘You indeed are dearer to me than my life, there is no doubt. But for you looking after your territory is indeed obligatory. (16)
uttara.72.17: ‘Therefore, O scion of the Kakutsthas, stay with me for seven nights and then you should proceed to Madhurā with attendants, army and carriers.’ (17)
uttara.72.18: Hearing these words of Śrī Rāma, spoken rightfully and in accordance with his Dharma, Śatrughna in a depressed tone spoke ‘So be it.’ (18)
uttara.72.19: As desired by the descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, Śatrughna, the mighty one, made himself ready to depart, having spent seven nights there. (19)
uttara.72.20: Taking leave of the noble Śrī Rāma of true valour, and also Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa, he ascended the marvellous chariot. (20)
uttara.72.21: Followed by the noble Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata on foot, for a long distance, Śatrughna sped in haste to the city, Madhupurī. (21)
uttara.73.1: Having despatched Śatrughna, the descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, together with the two brothers lived happily and contented, ruling rightfully over his kingdom. (1)
uttara.73.2: Then after a few days an old Brāhmaṇa citizen of Ayodhyā, carrying his dead son’s body, appeared at the royal gate. (2)
uttara.73.4: Filled with affection and sorrow, and crying, pronounced these words (exclamations) repeatedly ‘O son ! O son ! What evil deed have I committed in my former birth that I should see my only son dead. (3-4)
uttara.73.5: ‘O son, you have met with death untimely, having not reached adolescence and being a child of merely five thousand days (less than fourteen years) which leads to my sorrow. (5)
uttara.73.6: ‘O son, I, alongwith your mother, shall meet with death in a few days, there is no doubt about it. (6)
uttara.73.7: ‘I do not remember having spoken untruth, nor, even ever having committed sinful acts with regard to all beings. (7)
uttara.73.8: ‘Due to what evil deed, my own son, although a child, has gone away to the abode of Yama, the son of Vivasvān, without having performed the paternal rites (our last rites). (8)
uttara.73.9: ‘I have neither seen nor heard of such untimely death, of immature type, in the territory of Śrī Rāma. (9)
uttara.73.10: ‘There is no doubt that there must have been some evil deed performed by Śrī Rāma due to which indeed death meets the children in his territory. (10)
uttara.73.11: ‘There is no fear of death for the children in other territories. So, O king, bring back to life this child, possessed by death. (11)
uttara.73.12: ‘At the very royal gate, I shall lay down my life with my wife, like an orphan, O Śrī Rāma; you be happy having committed the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa. (12)
uttara.73.13: ‘You will attain longlife with your brothers: till now we have lived happily in your kingdom, O mighty one. (13)
uttara.73.14: ‘This death of my son has befallen on me. Therefore, O Śrī Rāma, staying under you we are under the sway of death, and there is little chance of happiness now. (14)
uttara.73.15: ‘Presently the reign of the noble Ikṣvākus is rendered orphan; now having accepted Śrī Rāma as the master, in whose reign certainly children’s death will occur. (15)
uttara.73.16: ‘The subjects, who are not protected rightfully, perish on account of the faults of the kings; when the king is not rightful, the people die untimely. (16)
uttara.73.17: ‘Whatever impropriety is committed by men in towns and provinces, and if there is no protection from them, then there is indeed such untimely destruction by death. (17)
uttara.73.18: ‘Both in the towns and provinces it is clear that there must have been some fault in the king, there is no doubt, due to which this death of my son has occurred.’ (18)
uttara.73.19: Thus making such pitiful utterances again and again and keeping in check the King, inflicted by sorrow, he embraced the dead child repeatedly. (19)
uttara.74.1: The scion of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma, heard all the pitiful lamentations of that Brāhmaṇa, full of pain and sorrow. (1)
uttara.74.2: Inflicted by pain He, Śrī Rāma, called His councillors, Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva and also his brothers, together with the citizens. (2)
uttara.74.3: Then eight Brāhmaṇas together with Vasiṣṭha were made to appear before the King comparable with the gods, and they said ‘victory to you.’ (3)
uttara.74.4: Mārkaṇḍeya, Maudgalya, Vāmadeva, Kaśyapa, Kātyāyana, Jābāli, Gautama and Nārada were made to enter. (4)
uttara.74.10: These excellent Brāhmaṇas were all provided with seats. The councillors and citizens all were suitably seated after all those effulgent ones had taken their seats. The descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, having saluted the great sages with folded hands, conveyed to them: ‘This Brāhmaṇa obstructs the royal gate. Nārada hearing those words of the King in grief, replied with these opportune words in the presence of the sages; ‘Listen, O King, how the death of child has taken place untimely. Hearing what I say, O king, descendant of Raghu, do what requires to be done. In the Kṛtayuga formerly the Brāhmaṇas alone were performers of austerities; no non-Brāhmaṇas ever practised austerities in that Yuga, inflamed by penances, and dominated by Brāhmaṇa, and also there was no prevalence of ignorance. All were born immortal ones and also possessed of distant vision; then came the Tretāyuga for men possessed of mortal frame. (5—10)
uttara.74.12: . ‘In Tretā, strongly built Kṣatriyas were dominant and practised austere penance. But those of Kṛtayuga were certainly superior in merit to those who belonged to Tretā (11-12)
uttara.74.14: ‘In Kṛtayuga Brāhmaṇas were superior and Kṣatriyas were inferior in the merits of austerity and effulgence but in Tretā both became equal and at par. (13-14)
uttara.74.16: ‘Tretā is dominated by Varṇāśrama Dharma. But here itself irreligion had stepped in even though on one foot, yet hereafter gradually there will be decline in Dharma. (15-16)
uttara.74.17: ‘The Rājasika acts like agriculture was known to be low (अनृत) and was supposed to be not recommendable. The same act in the form of a foot of irreligion was firmly rooted on the earth in Tretā. (17)
uttara.74.18: “This way by establishing one of his fruit in the shape of falsehood, the irreligion limited the life span of beings in Tretā in comparison to Satyayuga. (18)
uttara.74.19: ‘Therefore in order to save themselves from the evil effect of falsehood, one foot of irreligion, people who were dedicated to truthful conduct scrupulously practised fully auspicious deeds. (19)
uttara.74.21: ‘Yet in Tretā only Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas engaged themselves in observing penance. The rest of the people did servicing (like production and manual labour) out of these four categories the Vaiśyas and Śūdras got as their share—the service as their own Dharma. Śūdras particularly served and adored the other three castes. (20-21)
uttara.74.22: ‘O best among the kings, in the meanwhile the Tretā approaches its end, the Vaiśyas and Śūdras indulge in irreligion through falsehood as one of its feet. Then Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas suffer more and more deterioration. (22)
uttara.74.23: ‘Then unrighteousness placed on the earth its second foot, and by that the third Yuga was counted as Dvāpara (given to two feet). (23)
uttara.74.24: “With the coming into existence of the Dvāparayuga, unrighteousness and Anṛta (अनृत) flourished, O bull among men. (24)
uttara.74.25: ‘In this Yuga, known as Dvāpara, penance entered the Vaiśya, thus through the three Yugas penance entered the three Varṇas (classes) successively. (25)
uttara.74.26: ‘Righteousness was established in these three Yugas resorting to the three Varṇas (classes), the Śūdra could not attain the right of penance in these Yugas, O bull among men. (26)
uttara.74.27: ‘O best among kings, one belonging to lower caste performs severe penances. In the future Kali age the performance of penance will go to Śūdra. (27)
uttara.74.28: ‘Even in Dvāpara, penance by a Śūdra is taken to be great irreligion. (Now in Tretā surely) some Śūdra is engaged in severe penance in some frontier province—the wreched one. (28)
uttara.74.30: ‘This infantile death is the result of the same. If some one practises Adharma in the territory of a King, it causes a great loss to the state prosperity and the king goes to hell; there is no doubt about it. (29-30)
uttara.74.33: ‘Righteously ruling over the subjects, the king shares one sixth portion of the merit that accrues due to pious deeds performed by study and penance, why should partaker of one sixth not protect the subjects? So you, O lion among kings, investigate your territory. Wherever you see unrighteous actions done, then make efforts to put them right; thus righteousness and long life will prevail among men, O best among men, and also the child will come back to life.’ (31—33)
uttara.75.1: Hearing those nectar-like words of Nārada, Śrī Rāma was highly pleased and spoke thus to Lakṣmaṇa: (1)
uttara.75.2: ‘O gracious one, go and console the best among Brāhmaṇas, and place the body of the dead child in an oil tub. (2)
uttara.75.3: ‘O gracious one, provide it (the tub) with lasting and fragrant oils, so that the body of the child may not decompose. (3)
uttara.75.4: ‘Make arrangements to preserve the body of the child, the innocent one, so that it may not get decomposed and the limbs are not disjointed.’ (4)
uttara.75.5: Having thus told the auspicious Lakṣmaṇa, the scion of the Kakutsthas, Śrī Rāma summoned mentally Puṣpaka: ‘Come O famous one.’ (5)
uttara.75.6: Puṣpaka, adorned with gold, taking the hint came at once near the descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma. (6)
uttara.75.7: The Puṣpaka spoke bending down, to Śrī Rāma: ‘O King of long arms, here I am, your servant, at your command.’ (7)
uttara.75.8: Hearing these appealing words of the Puṣpaka, the king, Śrī Rāma, having saluted the great sages, ascended the plane. (8)
uttara.75.10: Taking His bow and quiver and a dazzling sword, and leaving both Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata in the city, He went looking here and there to the western direction full of greenery and then proceeded to the northern direction covered by the snow-clad mountain, Himālaya. (9-10)
uttara.75.11: Seeing not the slightest unrighteous thing done there, then He, Śrī Rāma, scanned also the whole eastern region. (11)
uttara.75.13: The King, Śrī Rāma, then seated on the Puṣpaka, saw the southern quarter, where conduct was the purest, and which was as clear as the base of mirror, He saw on the northern side of the Śaivala mountain a great lake. (12-13)
uttara.75.14: In that lake the descendant of Raghu, the noble one, saw an ascetic performing great penances, while suspended with head turned downward. (14)
uttara.75.15: The son of Raghu, the kind one, Śrī Rāma, having approached that ascetic, performing great penances, said to him: ‘O performer of vows, you are great. (15)
uttara.75.16: ‘O powerful one, aged through penances, to which caste do you belong, I ask you out of curiosity. I am Rāma, son of King Daśaratha. (16)
uttara.75.17: ‘What object is desired by you to be obtained as boon, is it the attainment of the heaven or some other object, for which you perform penances, difficult to be performed by others? (17)
uttara.75.18: ‘For which object have you practised penances, that I want to hear, O ascetic? Are you a Brāhmaṇa? O good man, may welfare be with you, are you a Kṣatriya difficult to overcome, or belonging to the third caste, a Vaiśya, or a Śūdra? Please speak out the truth.’ (18)
uttara.75.19: Thus enquired by the King, the son of Daśaratha, King of Kings, that ascetic spoke of his own caste and reason for practising the penances.’ (19)
uttara.76.1: Hearing those words of Śrī Rāma capable of doing anything with ease, remaining with the head downwards, he (the ascetic) replied: (1)
uttara.76.2: ‘O famous one, I am born in the line of the Śūdra caste, and have resorted to great penance. I desire godhood, O Śrī Rāma, with this body. (2)
uttara.76.3: ‘I do not speak untruth as I wish to conquer the world of the gods, know me as Śūdra, Śambūka by name, O scion of the Kakutsthas, Śrī Rāma.’ (3)
uttara.76.4: On this the descendant of Raghu, taking out dazling sword from its sheath, chopped off the head of the Śūdra, while he was speaking thus. (4)
uttara.76.5: On the Śūdra being killed, the gods headed by Agni together with Indra repeatedly praised the scion of the Kakutsthas saying: ‘Well done.’ (5)
uttara.76.6: A shower of very fragrant divine flowers, carried by the wind, fell from all sides. (6)
uttara.76.7: The gods highly pleased said to Śrī Rāma of true valour: ‘O king, O wise one, you have done this wonderful job for gods. (7)
uttara.76.8: ‘Take whatever boon you desire, O Subjugator of foes, due to your good deed this Śūdra will not attain heaven, O descendant of Raghu’. (8)
uttara.76.9: Hearing the words of the gods, Śrī Rāma of true valour spoke to Indra the destroyer of enemy fortresses thus: (9)
uttara.76.10: “If the gods are pleased, may that son of the Brāhmaṇa come back to life, grant me this boon, this is the best and most coveted boon for me. (10)
uttara.76.11: “The only child of the Brāhmaṇa was taken to the abode of Yama, the son of Vivasvān, untimely due to my some wrongful doing. (11)
uttara.76.12: “So please bring the child to life again, may welfare be with you. ‘I shall bring your child back to life,’ thus I have promised to the Brāhmaṇa. May my words not be untrue.” (12)
uttara.76.13: Hearing these words of Śrī Rāma, the best among the gods, highly pleased, replied to the descendant of Raghu: (13)
uttara.76.14: ‘Be contended, O Scion of Kakutstha, that child has come back to life and joined his kinsmen. (14)
uttara.76.15: ‘The moment the Śūdra was killed, that very moment this child came to life. (15)
uttara.76.16: ‘Hail to Thee, we wish your welfare; now we may proceed, O bull among men, O descendant of Raghu, we wish to see the hermitage of Agastya. (16)
uttara.76.17: ‘The brilliant one, the initiation (vow) of that Ṛṣi (sage) among Brāhmaṇas, Agastya, has come to an end, twelfth year he has passed observing the vow of sleeping on the water. (17)
uttara.76.18: ‘Therefore, O scion of Kakutstha, we shall go to applaud the sage, you too should go to see that great sage; we wish your welfare!’ (18)
uttara.76.19: ‘The descendant of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma, having promised to do so, ascended the chariot, Puṣpaka, ornamented with gold. (19)
uttara.76.20: Then the gods proceeded on spacious Vimānas, planes : Śrī Rāma too followed them soon to the hermitage of the pitcher-born, Agastya. (20)
uttara.76.21: Seeing the gods arrived, Agastya, the repository of penances, the holy one, worshipped all of them without discrimination. (21)
uttara.76.22: Accepting the worship and adoring the great sage, Agastya, the gods highly pleased went away to the upper-most heaven together with their followers. (22)
uttara.76.23: After the gods had departed, the scion of Kakutstha descending from Puṣpaka, made obeisance to the great sage, Agastya. (23)
uttara.76.24: Śrī Rāma paid obeisance to the noble sage, effulgent with the Tapa of austerity and having received the best hospitality, took his seat. (24)
uttara.76.25: Agastya, the sage of great penances, said to Śrī Rāma : ‘Welcome to you, best among men, O descendant of Raghu, it is my fortune that you have come. (25)
uttara.76.26: “By your excellent virtues you are worthy of adoration as my honoured guest, O king, you always dwell in my heart. (26)
uttara.76.27: “The gods say that You have come here after killing the Śūdra and by your righteous act, (of killing the Śūdra) You have thus restored to life the son of the Brāhmaṇa. (27)
uttara.76.29: “Stay one night with me, O descendant of Raghu, You are Nārāyaṇa (the abode of all souls), and all is established in You. You are lord of all the gods, the eternal Puruṣa, You may, indeed, go back to your city at dawn. (28-29)
uttara.76.30: “This divine ornament glowing with its own divine lusture, O gracious one, has been made by Viśvakarmā (the divine artisan). (30)
uttara.76.31: “Please accept this, O scion of Kakutstha, for my pleasure, a gift when offered again constitutes great merit. (31)
uttara.76.34: “You are worthy of wearing this ornament. You indeed are capable of giving precious gifts, and also protecting the gods together with Indra. Therefore, duly I give this to you, please accept it.” The wisest among the wise, the great charioteer of Ikṣvāku dynasty, Śrī Rāma while aware of his Kṣatriya duties, asked the Mahātmā: “Sir, accepting donation is not prohibited only for Brāhmaṇas. (32—34)
uttara.76.36: “O best among the Brāhmaṇas, it is strictly prohibited for the Kṣatriya to accept any charitable gift. It is more so in case a Brāhmaṇa is the donor. Kindly explain.” Having been thus enquired by Śrī Rāma, the great sage Agastya said in reply: (35-36)
uttara.76.37: “O Śrī Rāma! In the times during the Satyayuga, an age of Brahma, all the subjects were without a king. Later on Indra was declared as king of gods. (37)
uttara.76.39: Then people went to god Brahmā in order to have a king and prayed to him, ‘O Lord, you have appointed Indra as king of gods. Similarly, for us also provide a worthy man as our king, so that worshipping him we could move about in the world, becoming free of sins. (38-39)
uttara.76.41: ‘We shall not live without a king, This is our supreme decision.’ Then Brahmā, the highest god, after calling the guardians of regions alongwith Indra, said: ‘All of you give me a portion of your authority.’ Then all the guardians gave away a portion of their power. (40-41)
uttara.76.42: ‘Then Brahmā sneezed, whence was born king Kṣupa. Brahmā invested him with the entire might of the guardians (of regions given away by them). (42)
uttara.76.43: Then he made Kṣupa the ruling king of the people. Kṣupa after becoming king ruled the earth by virtue of the portion of the might given by Indra. (43)
uttara.76.51: The king nourished the people by the portion of power given to him by Varuṇa. By the portion of the mighty Kubera, he then, lent to the people the glory of Kubera, the Lord of riches. By the portion of Yama he devised punishment to the people as and when they committed sin(s). ‘O Śrī Rāma, the foremost among men! (as king, you are also invested with the might of the guardians of regions). For my deliverance accept this ornament through the portion (of the might) of Indra, O Lord ! Prosperity be unto you !’ Then Śrī Rāma accepted the divine ornament, bright like the sun, given by the high-souled hermit, and asked about his acquisition of the ornament. ‘O Eminent Brāhmaṇa ! How and from where did you acquire this divine and wonderful ornament? I am asking this out of curiosity, as you are a great repository of wonders.’ After Śrī Rāma enquired of, the sage said to Śrī Rāma, ‘Listen, O Śrī Rāma, what happened in the old Tretā age.’ (44—51)
uttara.77.1: “O Śrī Rāma! In the former Tretāyuga there was a forest, extending to hundred Yojanas, where there were neither animals nor birds. (1)
uttara.77.2: “In that forest, uninhabited by men, I practised askesis, which was the best of penances, O gracious one ! I set my foot to know all about the forest. (2)
uttara.77.3: “I could not indeed specify the beauty of that forest with its tasty fruits and roots and groves of various types. (3)
uttara.77.4: “In the midst of the forest was a lake, one Yojana wide; filled with swans and ducks and beautified with Cakrawāka birds. (4)
uttara.77.7: “The lake was full of lotuses and water-lilies with no trace of moss, it was a great wonder, enjoyable and excelled by none, it was clear like crystal and calm and inhabited by innumerable lovely birds. Near that lake there was a strong, brilliant, wonderful hermitage, old and extremely holy; but not inhabited by the ascetics: There O bull among men ! I dwelt one summer night. (5—7)
uttara.77.8: “Rising in the early morning for daybreak-duties I reached the lake and then saw there a corpse (dead body) plump and spotless shining in the water. (8)
uttara.77.15: Pondering over it lying with all its beauty inside the lake, I, for a moment, O descendant of Raghu, stood apart and thought: O lord, what could this be. Then all at once I saw a divine and wonderful spacious chariot yoked by swans and having the speed of mind; O scion of Raghus! I saw a denizen of the heaven on that chariot, thousands of divinely ornamented nymphs served him, some were singing, others were melodiously playing on the Mṛdaṅga (drum), lute and Paṇava (symbol), and others were dancing; Some other with lotus-like eyes fanned his face with expensive chowries with gold-handles and the lustre comparable with the rays of the moon; Then raising himself up from the throne, as the sun rises on the summits of Meru mountain, he, the denizen of heaven getting down from the chariot ate up the corpse, while I looked on, O descendant of Raghu. (9—15)
uttara.77.16: “Then having consumed to his satisfaction, the flesh rich in fat, the celestial being, going down the lake performed ablutions. (16)
uttara.77.17: “Having sipped water (in ablution) in the prescribed way that celestial being, O descendant of Raghu, got ready to ascend the excellent chariot. (17)
uttara.77.18: “Seeing him, who was like a god, ascending the chariot, I, on my part, spoke to him these words: ‘O bull among men ! Who are you? O god-like one, O gracious one, You should tell me why you ate this loathsome food, looked down upon by others. (18)
uttara.77.20: “ ‘You possess ethereal beauty. Sir, whose food could be this; therefore, O gracious one, I am wonder-struck. I wish to know the facts. I do not consider this corpse as your food in expediency.’ (19-20)
uttara.77.21: “Thus spoken to out of curiosity and also in well-chosen words, the celestial one, O King, having heard me, narrated all that I had enquired.” (21)
uttara.78.1: Hearing the words comprised of holy syllables spoken by me, O descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, the celestial being, with folded hands replied thus: (1)
uttara.78.2: “O Brāhmaṇa ! listen to what happened formerly, that could not be resisted and which is the cause of my pleasure and sorrow, as you desire to know it. (2)
uttara.78.3: “In the old days, my father Vaidarbha of great fame was possessed of great power and was known in the three worlds by the name of Sudeva. (3)
uttara.78.4: “Two sons were born to him from his two wives. I, the elder one, was known as Śweta, while my younger brother was known as Suratha. (4)
uttara.78.5: “On my father having attained heaven, the citizens consecrated me. And I ruled righteously, with care. (5)
uttara.78.6: “O Brāhmaṇa, observer of vows, thus a thousand years passed by, with my ruling over the kingdom and protecting my subjects. (6)
uttara.78.8: “ So, O best among Brāhmaṇas, knowing from some men about the span of my life, keeping in mind the approach of death, I came and entered this forest near the beautiful lake, difficult to enter and with no animals or birds residing therein to perform penances. (7-8)
uttara.78.9: “Having consecrated Suratha as the king, and reaching this lake, I performed penances for long. (9)
uttara.78.10: “Practising severe austerities for three thousand years in this great forest, I obtained the world of Brahmā (heaven) excelling all other worlds. (10)
uttara.78.11: “Having reached the heaven, O best among Brāhmaṇas, great hunger and thirst pained me and my senses were badly afflicted. (11)
uttara.78.12: “Then approaching Brahmā the best in the three worlds, I said, ‘Sir, this world of Brahmā is free from hunger and thirst. (12)
uttara.78.13: “ ‘As a consequence of which actions I am afflicted by hunger and thirst? What my food is, O God? O Brahmā! please tell me that’. (13)
uttara.78.14: “On this Brahmā told me, ‘O son of Sudeva, your food is your own tasty flesh, eat that for ever. (14)
uttara.78.15: “You have well-nourished your own body performing the best of penances. That which is not sown, shall never sprout O wise one. (15)
uttara.78.16: “You have not given even the smallest thing in charity, and have only practised great penances. Therefore, having reached heaven hunger and thirst afflict you. (16)
uttara.78.17: “As you eat your own body, well-nourished by edibles, full of the flavour of nectar; therefore, by that (eating flesh) you will live. (17)
uttara.78.18: “When the great and unconquerable sage Agastya will come to that forest, O Śweta, you will be delivered of this trouble. (18)
uttara.78.19: “O gracious one, Agastya is capable of delivering even the host of gods, what to say of you, afflicted with hunger and thirst, O long-armed one! (19)
uttara.78.20: “Thus having learnt of the decision of the god of the gods, Brahmā, O best among men, I make food of my own body. (20)
uttara.78.21: “O Brāhmaṇa, this body does not exhaust, although enjoyed by me for many years, and O Ṛṣi! I am fully quenched too. (21)
uttara.78.22: “So deliver me—troubled one, from the difficulty. None other than Agastya, the pitcher-born ascetic, has power to do so. (22)
uttara.78.23: “O gracious one, best among Brāhmaṇas, accept this ornament for wearing, may welfare be with you. Please favour me by accepting this. (23)
uttara.78.24: “All this gold, wealth, apparel, edibles and enjoyables, O Ṛṣi among Brāhmaṇas, I offer you as also the ornaments. (24)
uttara.78.25: “All desirables and enjoyables also I surrender to you. I deserve to be favoured by you by releasing me of troubles.” (25)
uttara.78.26: ‘Having heard these words full of sorrow from the celestial one, I accepted this wonderful ornament for releaving him. (26)
uttara.78.28: ‘As soon as I accepted that auspicious ornament, the former body of the Ṛṣi among kings (Śweta) vanished and the Ṛṣi among kings, extremely happy and satisfied, went to the heaven. (27-28)
uttara.78.29: ‘By him (Śweta) equal to Indra, this divine ornament, of wonderful form, was given to me, O scion of Kakutstha, for that purpose.’ (29)
uttara.79.1: Hearing that most wonderful and marvellous story, narrated by Agastya, Śrī Rāma asked him again, full of dismay and reverence. (1)
uttara.79.2: “Sir, how was that fearful forest, where the Vaidarbhaka king Śweta was performing penances, devoid of animals and birds. (2)
uttara.79.3: “I wish to know in detail how that king entered that forest, which was barren and uninhabited by men, to perform penances.” (3)
uttara.79.4: Hearing the words of Śrī Rāma uttered out of curiosity, the highly powerful one, Agastya, spoke thus: (4)
uttara.79.5: “In the former Kṛtayuga, Manu (Vaivasvata) was the king. His son, a joy to his family, was the famous Ikṣvāku. (5)
uttara.79.6: “Placing the first son, Ikṣvāku, unconquerable on the earth, incharge of the kingdom, Manu said to him: ‘Be the progenitor of all royal families.’ (6)
uttara.79.7: “Then, O descendant of Raghu, the son promised to do so and being fully satisfied Manu addressed him thus. (7)
uttara.79.8: “O noble one, I am pleased, you will be the forerunner of all royal families, there is no doubt. By punishment as a sign of authority protect the subjects; do not mete out unnecessary punishments. (8)
uttara.79.9: “That form of punishment, which is meted out to the guilty men, being given in proper manner, leads the king to heaven. (9)
uttara.79.10: “Therefore, O dear son of long arms, make efforts to mete out punishment according to prescriptions in the Śāstras. Resorting to just punishment properly, you will attain great righteousness.” (10)
uttara.79.11: Thus, having instructed him, Manu, pleased with himself, went to the eternal abode of Brahmā through Samādhi (trance). (11)
uttara.79.12: When Manu had left for heaven, Ikṣvāku of unlimited brilliance, fell to thinking, ‘How shall I produce sons?’ (12)
uttara.79.13: Through true actions of many types, then the son of Manu, the pious one, procreated the hundred sons, comparable with the sons of the gods. (13)
uttara.79.15: The youngest one of them, was ignorant, and illiterate and did not serve his elders. His father gave him, dull-witted son, the name ‘Daṇḍa’, thinking that physical punishment shall certainly be the fate of this one (son). (14-15)
uttara.79.16: “Not seeing any territory fully fearful, the father gave him the kingdom situated between the Vindhya and Śaivala mountains. (16)
uttara.79.17: “That Daṇḍa became the king of that territory situated at the foot of the mountains and established a city unmatched and the best (among the cities). (17)
uttara.79.18: “Daṇḍa named the city Madhumanta, O lord, and chose as his chief priest Uśanā, rich in vows. (18)
uttara.79.19: “Thus that king, Daṇḍa, ruled over that kingdom together with the chief priest, the Kingdom being filled with joyful men as the king of gods rules in the heaven. (19)
uttara.79.20: “Then that King, Daṇḍa, the grandson of Manu, together with Uśana of great fame, ruled as a highly pious king, like Indra ruling over the gods.” (20)
uttara.80.1: Having thus narrated the story of Ikṣvāku to Śrī Rāma, the great sage, Agastya, the pitcher-born one, began to narrate another story connected with the same. (1)
uttara.80.2: ‘Then, O scion of Kakutstha, that Daṇḍa, the self-controlled one, ruled over that kingdom there, uprooting all foes, for successively ten thousand years. (2)
uttara.80.3: Then at one time the king, Daṇḍa, went to the beautiful hermitage of sage Bhārgava (Śukra), in the enjoyable month of Caitra. (3)
uttara.80.4: There Daṇḍa saw the daughter of Bhārgava, a paragon of beauty, roaming about in the forest. (4)
uttara.80.5: Having seen her, that wicked minded Daṇḍa, dull-witted, one afflicted by the arrows of cupid, greatly agitated approached the daughter of Bhārgava and said: (5)
uttara.80.6: ‘O one of beautiful hips and loins, wherefrom do you hail, O beautiful one ! whose daughter you are? O of auspicious face, afflicted as I am by cupid, I ask you.’ (6)
uttara.80.7: When he said so, blinded by the sexual urge and madly infatuated as he was, the daughter of Bhārgava replied thus courteously: (7)
uttara.80.8: ‘Know me as the daughter of the lord Bhārgava, unwearied in action, named Arajā, the eldest one residing in the hermitage. (8)
uttara.80.9: ‘Do not touch me by force, I am under the control of my father, O best among kings. My father is your preceptor and you are the pupil of that noble one. (9)
uttara.80.11: ‘Enraged, he (Bhārgava), the performer of great penances, shall cause you much grief. If, however, for something other than mere passion, you desire me, then ask my hand following the righteous path from my father, O best among men; otherwise you will meet with frightful consequences. (10-11)
uttara.80.12: ‘In anger my father would burn up the three worlds O one of perfect limbs. He will give me to you if asked for.’ (12)
uttara.80.13: To Arajā speaking thus, Daṇḍa under the power of cupid, intoxicated with passion, replied folding his hands over his head: (13)
uttara.80.14: ‘Please favour me, O one of beautiful hips and loins, do not delay, O beautiful one, my vital breaths are shattering on your account. (14)
uttara.80.15: ‘By possessing you, let there be my death, or a great sin committed, accept me, devoted to you and asking for you, highly agitated.’ (15)
uttara.80.16: Thus saying, he, Daṇḍa, the strong one, seizing the trembling daughter of Bhārgava between his arms by force, he raped her. (16)
uttara.80.17: Having committed that terrible heinous crime, he went back soon to the unparalleled Madhumanta. (17)
uttara.80.18: That Arajā too, remained weeping near the hermitage, and in great fright waited for her father, who was just like a god. (18)
uttara.81.1: Having heard the account of Arajā that gracious divine Ṛṣi Bhārgava came back at once to his hermitage surrounded by his pupils, although bitten by hunger. (1)
uttara.81.2: He saw the pitiable Arajā covered with semen, as the full-moon at dawn faded out due to being eclipsed. (2)
uttara.81.3: Anger flared up in him, specially as he was bitten by hunger, as if to burn the three worlds, and he said to his pupils: (3)
uttara.81.4: “See how this performer of action contrary to good conduct, and ignorant one meets with severe calamities produced by me in anger, and comparable with the flames of fire. (4)
uttara.81.5: “Destruction is the fate of that dull-witted one who wishes to touch the flames of the kindled fire. (5)
uttara.81.6: “As he has committed this heinous crime, so this dull-witted one will get the fruit of his sin. (6)
uttara.81.7: “In seven nights, this king, the dull-witted one, with his sons, army and carriers, and of sinful conduct, shall meet with death. (7)
uttara.81.8: “For a hundred Yojanas all round, the territory of this dull-witted one, the extirpator of Pāka, Indra shall burn up with a shower of dust. (8)
uttara.81.9: “All beings, stationary and moving, that are here, will perish due to this heavy shower of dust. (9)
uttara.81.10: “After seven nights, the prosperous territory of Daṇḍa will entirely disappear alongwith the shower of dust.” (10)
uttara.81.11: Thus speaking to the inhabitors of the hermitage, he, Bhārgava, possessed of red eyes with rage said to them again, ‘stay at the outskirts of this territory.’ (11)
uttara.81.12: Hearing these words of Uśanā, the Āśrama-dwellers, went out of his territory and made place for themselves elsewhere. (12)
uttara.81.13: Having thus spoken to the ascetics, Bhārgava then addressed Arajā, “O dull-witted, you will stay in this Āśrama, conscious of your duties. (13)
uttara.81.14: “O Arajā, free from worry, enjoy this lake of beautiful form and extending to a Yojana, and also wait for some time. (14)
uttara.81.15: “Those beings, who will come to stay near you for a night, will be unassailable forever by the shower of dust.” (15)
uttara.81.16: “On hearing the command of the Brahmarṣi, Arajā, the daughter of Bhṛgu, despite being very much pained said to her father “Very well.” (16)
uttara.81.19: “Having said this, Bhṛgu took up his abode elsewhere. That kingdom of the chief of the kings alongwith his servants, the army and the vehicles, was reduced to ashes within seven days, as was declared by the Brahmavādī Bhṛgu. This kingdom of Daṇḍa lying between the Vindhya and the Śaivala mountains, was cursed by the Brahmarṣi, since Daṇḍa had acted unrighteously. Since then, O descendant of Kakutstha, it has been called Daṇḍakāraṇya. (17—19)
uttara.81.20: “Since ascetics came and inhabited here it has been known as ‘Janasthāna’, O Rāma ! I have told you everything about what you enquired of me. (20)
uttara.81.22: “O Valiant one ! The time for the performance of Sandhyā is passing. All these great sages, O foremost among men ! after having finished their bath, are worshipping the sun, with their respective pitcher filled with water. The sun, having accepted the worship in the form of recitation of Vedic hymns by the knowers of Brahma, has set in. You also go and take bath and sip water and perform Sandhyā.” (21-22)
uttara.82.1: Having heard with reverence the words of the sage, Agastya, Śrī Rāma approached the holy lake inhabited by the host of Apsarās, for performing his evening adoration. (1)
uttara.82.2: Having sipped the water there and performed the evening Pūjā, Śrī Rāma entered the hermitage of Agastya, the holy pitcher-born one. (2)
uttara.82.3: Agastya offered to him for food radish of good quality and also purified rice and other edibles. (3)
uttara.82.4: That best among men, Śrī Rāma, enjoyed that food comparable with nectar, was highly pleased and satisfied. He spent that night together with the sage. (4)
uttara.82.5: Śrī Rāma, the best among the Raghus, the tamer of foes, getting up at dawn and having performed the morning daily rites, approached the sage to beg leave of him and to depart. (5)
uttara.82.6: Having saluted the great sage, born of the pitcher, Agastya, Śrī Rāma said to him: ‘I beg leave of you to depart to my own capital; may you permit me to do so. (6)
uttara.82.7: ‘I am fortunate having been favoured by seeing you. I shall come again to see you, O holy one, for purification of myself.’ (7)
uttara.82.8: While Rāma spoke in this marvellous manner, the great ascetic possessed of virtuous vision was highly pleased and said : (8)
uttara.82.9: ‘O Rāma, your speech of auspicious syllables is indeed wonderful, O descendant of Raghu, you are the purifier of all beings. (9)
uttara.82.10: ‘The few who see you even for a moment, are purified, and attain heaven, and are worshipped by the lord of heaven (gods). (10)
uttara.82.11: “Those beings on earth, who see you with inimical eyes, they are instantly struck by the rod of Yama and descend to hell. (11)
uttara.82.12: ‘O best among the Raghus, in this manner you are the purifier of all mortals, O scion of Raghu. The one describing Your sports (Līlās) on earth shall attain perfection. (12)
uttara.82.13: ‘You go with pleasure on your path unagitated and without fear and rule over your Kingdom righteously; you are the resort of this world.’ (13)
uttara.82.14: Thus spoken to by the sage, the king with folded and outstretched hands, the wise one, saluted that sage of truthful conduct. (14)
uttara.82.15: Saluting the best among sages, Agastya, and all other great ascetics, he ascended unagitated that Puṣpaka, ornamented with gold. (15)
uttara.82.16: The host of sages on all sides honoured him with blessings as the gods honour Indra, the thousand-eyed one. (16)
uttara.82.17: The well-composed Śrī Rāma on the Puṣpaka, ornamented with gold, looked like the moon near the cloud at the approach of the rainy season. (17)
uttara.82.18: Then, by the advent of midday, being honoured here and there, and having reached Ayodhyā, the scion of Kakutstha descended in the middle of the city. (18)
uttara.82.19: Then leaving the beautiful Puṣpaka, moving at will, He said: ‘Leaving me, go to Kubera, O powerful one; may welfare be with thee.’ (19)
uttara.82.20: Then Śrī Rāma hurriedly ordered the door-keeper in the other apartment : ‘Go to Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, those two of swift valour, and having conveyed to them my arrival, call them here, do not delay.’ (20)
uttara.83.1: Having heard the words of Śrī Rāma, who was unwearied in performance, the door-keeper called the two princes and they reported to the scion of Raghu. (1)
uttara.83.2: The scion of the Raghus seeing both the princes arrived, embraced them and then spoke to them these words : (2)
uttara.83.3: “I have done the service to the Brāhmaṇa as expected. Now I want to perform Rājasūya—the outer limit of piety, O brothers. (3)
uttara.83.4: “In my opinion the bridge of righteousness is imperishable and unchangeable; the discourse on righteousness destroys all sins. (4)
uttara.83.5: “Together with both of you, who are dear to me as myself, I wish to perform the excellent Rājasūya. Therein resides eternal righteousness. (5)
uttara.83.6: “The killer of foes, Mitra, attained the position of Varuṇa, having performed the Rājasūya with proper offerings and sacrifice. (6)
uttara.83.7: “The knower of Dharma (Law), Soma, having performed the Rājasūya, righteously, attained fame and eternal place in all the worlds. (7)
uttara.83.8: “Reflect on what is the best this day together with me, you two active ones should tell me what is good for the world and also what is proper for the future.” (8)
uttara.83.9: Hearing these words of the scion of Raghus, Śrī Rāma, Bharata, proficient in speaking, spoke thus, folding his hands: (9)
uttara.83.10: “O righteous one, in you is established the highest form of righteousness, this entire earth and all fame, O one of long arms and possessing uncomparable valour. (10)
uttara.83.11: “All kings like us, look upon Thee, O holy one, the lord of worlds as the gods look upon Prajāpati. (11)
uttara.83.12: “O King, O Raghunandana of mighty strength, all kings regard you as sons look to their fathers. You are the resort of this world and also of all beings, O scion of Raghu. (12)
uttara.83.13: “How, O king, you being so, wish to perform the Rājasūya sacrifice, in which there shall be the destruction of royal families on earth. (13)
uttara.83.14: “O King, those men, who on this earth are possessed of valour, all of them will be destroyed in that Yajña due to the anger of all. (14)
uttara.83.15: “O lion among men, possessed of unparalleled valour, accompanied with merits, it befits you not to destroy this earth, all indeed are under your sway.” (15)
uttara.83.17: Hearing these nectar-like words of Bharata, Śrī Rāma of true valour was extremely pleased and said these auspicious words to the enhancer of the joy of Kaikeyī, Bharata: ‘I am pleased and satisfied today at what you say, O sinless one. (16-17)
uttara.83.18: ‘These words spoken by you are potent and accompanied by righteousness. O tiger among men, as they relate to the protection of the earth. (18)
uttara.83.19: ‘I refrain, after what you have said, from the performance of the excellent sacrifice, Rājasūya, that was our intention, O Knower of Dharma (Law). (19)
uttara.83.20: ‘That action is not to be undertaken by the wise which causes pain to the worlds, O elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa. The words even of the young ones are worthy of acceptance if they are carrier of good. Therefore, I have listened to your sagacious talk, O mighty one; you have spoken so well.’ (20)
uttara.84.1: When Śrī Rāma and the noble Bharata had spoken thus, Lakṣmaṇa addressed these auspicious words to Śrī Rāma: (1)
uttara.84.2: “O descendant of Raghu, the great sacrifice, Aśvamedha, is the purifier of all sins and shall be your purifier, although difficult to perform, if you so please. (2)
uttara.84.3: “The legend about the very noble Vāsava (Indra) is heard, that Indra tainted by the sin of the killing of Brāhmaṇa was purified by the Horse-sacrifice. (3)
uttara.84.4: “In the ancient times, O one of long arms, in the struggle that ensued between the gods and demons, there happened to be the mighty Vṛtra, son of Diti, honoured by the worlds. (4)
uttara.84.5: “A hundred Yojanas horizontally and thrice in height, he out of affection for three worlds, looked on all beings with compassion. (5)
uttara.84.6: “Righteous and dutiful and well-composed in mind, he ruled over this wide earth righteously with great care. (6)
uttara.84.7: “In his reign the earth yielded all such desirable and flavoured things, as flowers, roots and fruits. (7)
uttara.84.8: “The earth belonging to him yielded forth fruits without being ploughed. He ruled over that sort of kingdom, prosperous with wonderful appearance. (8)
uttara.84.9: “It arose in his mind: ‘I shall perform the penance unequalled, penance is indeed the highest form of welfare; all other forms of happiness are out of illusions.’ (9)
uttara.84.10: “Leaving his eldest son, Madhureśwara, as in-charge of the citizens, he performed frightful penances, tormenting all gods. (10)
uttara.84.11: “On Vṛtra performing penances, Vāsava (Indra) being highly afraid, approaching Viṣṇu spoke thus, indeed. (11)
uttara.84.12: “ ‘O one of long arms, all the worlds have been conquered by him performing penances, he is righteous and powerful, I cannot subdue him. (12)
uttara.84.13: “ ‘If again he performs penances, all beings of the worlds will be under him. (13)
uttara.84.14: “ ‘O powerful one, you are overlooking this demon, O lord of the gods, if you are in anger, Vṛtra will not stand even for a moment. (14)
uttara.84.15: “ ‘Ever since you patronised him, he has attained supremacy over the worlds. (15)
uttara.84.16: “So, have mercy on the worlds now; by your favour, indeed, this world will be free from pain. (16)
uttara.84.17: “These denizens of heaven (gods) look upon Thee, O Viṣṇu, please help them by killing the mighty Vṛtra. (17)
uttara.84.18: “By you forever succour was given to the noble ones i.e., gods. For others these ignoble Asuras are unbearable. You, Sir, are the resort of those who have no shelter.” (18)
uttara.85.1: Hearing those words of Lakṣmaṇa, the extirpator of foes, Śrī Rāma, said: ‘O observer of vows, narrate in totality the killing of Vṛtra.’ (1)
uttara.85.2: Being thus spoken to by the scion of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, the enhancer of the joy of Sumitrā, Lakṣmaṇa, the observer of vows, narrated the divine story of the killing of Vṛtra again. (2)
uttara.85.3: ‘Having heard the words of the thousand-eyed one, Indra, and also of all the gods, Viṣṇu spoke thus to all the gods headed by Indra. (3)
uttara.85.4: ‘Formerly I was attached affectionately to Vṛtra here and thus for your good indeed I am not killing the great Asura. (4)
uttara.85.5: ‘That which leads to your great happiness, has indeed to be performed: Therefore, I shall tell you the means by which Vṛtra will be killed; the thousand-eyed one, Indra, will kill Vṛtra. (5)
uttara.85.6: ‘O best among gods, I shall divide myself threefold, by that the thousand-eyed one, Indra, will indeed kill Vṛtra. There is no doubt about it. (6)
uttara.85.7: ‘One part of mine may go to Vāsava (Indra), the second part may enter the thunderbolt and third, the earth; then Indra shall kill Vṛtra.’ (7)
uttara.85.8: On the lord of gods, Viṣṇu, speaking thus, the gods then said: ‘This is as You say, there is no doubt, O killer of the Daityas, sons of Diti. (8)
uttara.85.9: ‘Let welfare be with You, we shall now depart desiring the killing of the Asura, Vṛtra. O extremely liberal one, Viṣṇu, may you bestow Vāsava with your power.’ (9)
uttara.85.10: Then all the noble ones headed by the thousand-eyed god, Indra, went to that forest where the great Asura, Vṛtra, was. (10)
uttara.85.11: They saw the mighty Asura possessed of his own power performing penance, as if drinking the three worlds and burning up the sky. (11)
uttara.85.12: On seeing the best of Asuras, gods were frightened, and thought ‘how shall we kill him, and how indeed we shall not be conquered by him?’ (12)
uttara.85.13: While the gods were thus contemplating, the thousand-eyed one, the destroyer of fortress, Indra, taking hold of the thunderbolt with both of his hands, hurled it at the head of Vṛtra. (13)
uttara.85.14: When the head of Vṛtra struck by the thunderbolt, blazing like fire of destruction and inflamed by its own lustre, fell down, it simultaneously terrified the whole universe. (14)
uttara.85.15: The lord of the gods, possessed of fame, Indra, thinking that the killing of Vṛtra was not proper, fled soon to the ends of the earth out of fear. (15)
uttara.85.16: The slaughter of a Brāhmaṇa pursued Indra, fleeing fast and pervaded his limbs; sorrow came upon Indra. (16)
uttara.85.17: With their foe killed, and bereft of Indra, the gods, with Agni at their head, worshipped Viṣṇu, the lord of the three worlds again and again. (17)
uttara.85.18: ‘O mightiest of all, you are the resort, and being born first, the father of this earth, you assumed the form of Viṣṇu for the protection of all beings. (18)
uttara.85.19: ‘By you Vṛtra is killed; the slaughter of a Brāhmaṇa afflicts Vāsava (Indra), O lion among gods. Kindly arrange for his deliverance.’ (19)
uttara.85.20: Hearing those words of the gods, Viṣṇu said “Let Indra worship me, I shall purify the carrier of the thunderbolt. (20)
uttara.85.21: “Having propitiated me through the holy Aśvamedha, the humbler of Pāka, Indra, shall again attain the position of Indra among the gods, without fear from anywhere.” (21)
uttara.85.22: Thus pronouncing those nectar-like words before the gods, the lord of the gods, Viṣṇu, being eulogized by the gods, proceeded to heaven. (22)
uttara.86.2: That Lakṣmaṇa, having narrated the whole episode of the slaying of Vṛtra, proceeded to describe the remaining part of the story. On, Vṛtra of mighty power, a terror to the gods, being killed, Indra, the killer of Vṛtra, afflicted by the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter, became unconscious. (1-2)
uttara.86.3: Deprived of consciousness, he (Indra) went beyond the border of the world, where he remained for sometime as if writhing like a snake. (3)
